set_aside.subject: authorization scope of deliverer operations
set_aside.text: every operation on a project needs the token
set_aside.question: Which of the three operations count as being "on a project"—particularly "deliver one photo" and "record its publication"—and therefore require a token?
options: All three operations require a token because every photo and publication record belongs to a project.
Only scanning is necessarily a project operation; photo delivery and publication recording require a token only if their requests explicitly identify a project.
The text must define project-scoping separately for each operation.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat all three operations as project-scoped and require a token for each.

witness.initial: A confirmed project has a scanned photo ready for delivery.
events: The calling flow invokes deliver-one-photo using the photo reference but no explicit project identifier or token.
After publication, the calling flow invokes record-publication using the Portal photo id without a token.
outcomes: The service rejects both calls because the photo and publication mark belong to a project.
The service accepts them because neither operation's request is explicitly framed as an operation on a project.
witness.observer: The owner sees either failed delivery or a delivered and recorded photo.

set_aside.subject: token authorization model
set_aside.text: every operation on a project needs the token
set_aside.question: Must the token merely be present, must it be valid globally, or must it be authorized for the particular project being operated on?
options: One valid service token authorizes operations on every project.
Each project has or is bound to its own token, and the service verifies that binding.
A caller token is checked against an authorization policy that explicitly grants access to the named project.
set_aside.default_guess: Require a valid caller token whose authorization includes the specific project.

witness.initial: Two confirmed projects, A and B, exist, and the caller possesses a token accepted for project A.
events: The caller submits a scan or delivery operation for project B using the token accepted for A.
outcomes: The operation succeeds because the service only requires a valid token.
The operation fails because the token is not authorized for project B.
witness.observer: The caller and owner see whether project B can be scanned or delivered.
